skills/3-weekly/skills-army-hq/references/recovery.md — portable payload vs ignored machine-local state

nodes.label: Canonical owning repositories
nodes.description: Only authoring sources. A deployed payload that is ahead of its source must be preserved and landed upstream before it is redistributed.

nodes.label: Forge canonical drift gate
nodes.description: Compares Forge-owned deployed SKILL.md files with canonical tiered sources. Sync warns in preview and refuses deployment on drift unless explicitly overridden loudly.

nodes.label: Skills Army intake / update
nodes.description: Copies a reviewed skill folder from its owning local Git repository into the publisher's Pulse collection and records source commit/digest provenance.

nodes.label: Device A Pulse checkout / Deployed Skills
nodes.description: The publisher device's one deployed collection and portable payload tree. It is a generated distribution, not a second authoring source.

nodes.label: Device A local deployment state
nodes.description: Distinct collection identity, ownership receipts, target configuration, locks, backups and staging. Ignored and untracked; never transported to another device.

nodes.label: Device A app skill roots
nodes.description: Selected app directories point directly into Device A's Pulse collection. Discovery/runtime verification remains app-specific.

nodes.label: Reviewed Git commit / push / pull
nodes.description: Portable payload changes are committed and pushed from one designated publisher, then pulled only into clean consumer checkouts. The repository does not prove the currently installed scheduler implementation.

nodes.label: Private Git Pulse remote
nodes.description: Carries skill folders, manager scripts, README and tracked ignore policy. It must not carry receipts, target choices, locks, history, backups or staging.

nodes.label: Device B Pulse checkout / Deployed Skills
nodes.description: Pulled payloads are adopted in place; no second ~/Documents/Deployed Skills mirror is created. Existing links read new bytes immediately after a clean pull.

nodes.label: In-place adoption + local sync
nodes.description: Verifies clean tracked payloads, ignored machine state and portable manager links; creates only local receipts/targets, then reconciles owned app symlinks.

nodes.label: Device B local deployment state
nodes.description: A new collection identity and this device's own targets, receipts, locks, catalog/history, backups and staging. Nothing is copied from Device A's local state.

nodes.label: Device B app skill roots
nodes.description: Selected app directories point directly into Device B's Pulse collection. Foreign folders and retargeted links are preserved.

legend_note: GH-672 supersedes the GH-508 separate-projection design: each Pulse-enabled device has exactly one deployed collection inside its own checkout. Portable skill payloads travel through Git; local deployment state never does. Publication is shown as an explicit external workflow because the current repository cannot attest this machine's installed scheduler configuration.
